findings.fix: Consolidate duplicate variations using 301 redirects or canonicalize them to a single authoritative URL.

findings.title: robots.txt Presence & Accessibility

evidence.snippet:
Sitemap: https://docs.python.org/sitemap.xml

# Prevent development and old documentation from showing up in search results.
User-agent: *
Disallow: /dev
Disallow: /release

# Disallow EOL versions
Di

findings.why_it_matters: robots.txt is the universal entry point for all web crawlers. Without it, crawlers may waste crawl budget on non-canonical URLs, internal search parameters, or private endpoints.
findings.fix: Create a valid /robots.txt file at your domain root following RFC 9309 with User-agent, Disallow, and Sitemap directives.

findings.title: Accidental Critical Path Blocking in robots.txt

evidence.message: No catastrophic global Disallow: / rule found.

findings.why_it_matters: Accidental 'Disallow: /' or disallowing core CSS/JS/images prevents search engines and AI crawlers from indexing content or rendering pages properly.
findings.fix: Audit Disallow rules in robots.txt to ensure the homepage ('/') and primary content paths remain accessible.

findings.title: XML Sitemap Discovery & Validity
findings.why_it_matters: XML sitemaps provide a roadmap of all canonical, high-value pages, ensuring search engines discover new and updated content rapidly.
findings.fix: Publish an XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml and reference it in /robots.txt.

findings.title: www vs. non-www Redirection Consistency
findings.why_it_matters: Allowing both www and non-www versions of a website to return 200 OK splits link authority and creates duplicate content across domains.
findings.fix: Configure web server or CDN (Cloudflare/Vercel) to redirect the non-canonical host with a 301 status.

findings.title: Low readability score (18/100): Content is very difficult to read
findings.why_it_matters: Content that is unnecessarily convoluted or dense scores poorly with human readers and increases the risk that AI models hallucinate or misinterpret factual claims.
findings.fix: Aim for a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50–70 (accessible to general audiences) by shortening sentences and replacing bureaucratic jargon with plain language.

findings.title: Thin Content Pages (<250 Words)
findings.why_it_matters: Pages with less than 250 words offer little unique value to users, are flagged as low-quality under Google's Helpful Content guidelines, and are ignored by generative AI answer engines.
findings.fix: Expand thin pages with comprehensive answers, examples, or consolidate into parent category pages.

findings.title: Answer-First Structure (Inverted Pyramid)

evidence.snippet: welcome! this is the official documentation for python 3.15.2....

findings.why_it_matters: Generative AI models and featured snippet extractors strongly favor content that provides a direct, succinct answer in the opening 100–150 words rather than burying conclusions.
findings.fix: Open informational articles with a clear definition, immediate summary, or direct answer to the primary query before delving into history or background.

findings.title: Subheadings rarely use question formulations (missed generative search alignment)
findings.why_it_matters: Subheadings phrased as direct user questions ('How do I...', 'What is...', 'Why does...') strongly align with prompt formulations in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.
findings.fix: Structure H2 and H3 subheadings around real natural language questions users ask.

findings.title: FAQ content detected without FAQPage structured data markup

evidence.message: FAQ content detected in text, but no FAQPage schema is present.

findings.why_it_matters: Content structured as questions and answers benefits from FAQPage Schema markup, providing explicit question-answer tuples directly digestible by AI models.
findings.fix: Add FAQPage or HowTo JSON-LD schema markup to pages containing Q&A sections.

findings.title: Factual & Statistical Evidence Density
findings.why_it_matters: Generative answer engines (Perplexity, ChatGPT Search, Claude) favor content that contains concrete data points, statistics, dates, and named studies over generic hand-waving.
findings.fix: Ground claims in empirical statistics, specific percentages, dates, and named primary sources.

findings.title: Authoritative Outbound Citations
findings.why_it_matters: Outbound citations to authoritative external primary sources (.gov, .edu, Wikipedia, official docs) signal thorough research, build domain trust, and match citation networks indexed by LLMs.
findings.fix: Cite primary institutional, scientific, or official vendor documentation when stating facts.

findings.title: Visible Author Bylines & E-E-A-T Signals
findings.why_it_matters: Google's Search Quality Rater Guidelines (E-E-A-T: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) emphasize named authorship. AI answer engines prioritize content written by identifiable subject matter experts.
findings.fix: Add named author bylines linked to biographical profiles detailing credentials and experience.

findings.title: Missing rel='canonical' Link Tag
findings.why_it_matters: Without an explicit canonical tag, search engines must guess which version of a page to index, leading to duplicate content dilution across trailing slashes, HTTP/HTTPS, and query params.
findings.fix: Add a self-referencing <link rel='canonical' href='https://...'> tag in the <head>.

findings.title: Missing or Empty <title> Tag
findings.why_it_matters: The <title> tag is one of the most critical on-page ranking signals and provides the clickable headline in search engine results and AI answer cards.
findings.fix: Add a unique, descriptive <title> tag inside the <head> of every HTML page.

findings.title: Title tag is too short (<30 characters)
findings.why_it_matters: Titles under 30 characters underutilize ranking keywords; titles over 65 characters get truncated in SERPs (or rewritten by Google).
findings.fix: Format titles to be between 30 and 65 characters (approx. 200–600 pixels).

findings.title: Missing Meta Description
findings.why_it_matters: Meta descriptions provide the summary snippet in search results and help AI crawlers understand page intent before full parsing.
findings.fix: Add an enticing, descriptive <meta name='description' content='...'> tag.

findings.title: Meta description length (34 chars) is outside optimal range (70–160 chars)
findings.why_it_matters: Descriptions shorter than 70 characters offer poor click-through incentive; descriptions over 160 characters get truncated in search snippets.
findings.fix: Craft meta descriptions to be between 70 and 160 characters with a clear value proposition.

findings.title: H1 Heading Presence & Singularity
findings.why_it_matters: Every indexable page should have exactly one descriptive <h1> tag serving as the main topic header for users, search crawlers, and screen readers.
findings.fix: Ensure each page contains exactly one <h1> element accurately describing the page subject.

findings.title: Heading Hierarchy Level Skips
findings.why_it_matters: Skipping heading levels (e.g. from H1 directly to H3 or H4) breaks semantic document outlines, harming accessibility and confusing automated passage extractors.
findings.fix: Nest headings logically in descending order: H1 -> H2 -> H3.

findings.title: Core Schema.org Type Coverage
findings.why_it_matters: No Schema.org entity types were detected on this page.
findings.fix: Deploy relevant Schema.org JSON-LD templates based on page intent.

findings.title: Time to First Byte (TTFB) Latency
findings.why_it_matters: High server response latency slows down crawling, burns crawl budget, degrades Core Web Vitals, and causes AI bots with short timeout thresholds (e.g. 800ms) to abort requests.
findings.fix: Optimize database queries, enable server-side caching, and utilize edge CDNs (Cloudflare/Fastly).

findings.title: Mobile Responsive Viewport Configuration
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile-first indexing requires a responsive viewport tag so pages render correctly across smartphones, tablets, and mobile crawlers.
findings.fix: Add <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'> in the <head>.

findings.title: Missing recommended security headers (HSTS / nosniff)
findings.why_it_matters: Security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options) protect visitors from clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and man-in-the-middle downgrade attacks.
findings.fix: Configure web server or CDN to send Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options headers.
